name: Shiva amygdala signal (normal speed)
origin: Shiva software by Todd Murphy (signal templates licensed from Persinger and Koren)
summary: Murphy's simple Shiva session: the amygdala burst-firing signal stepped counter-clockwise around the head at the speed Murphy says 'was found to be the most effective in earlier lab studies'. The vendor presents it for emotional effects.
notes: Coils sit on Murphy's Shiva ring (Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2; one coil per site instead of Shiva's coil pairs) and step counter-clockwise seen from above, with Murphy's lecture example of 10, 12 ... 20 ms per coil (about 8 rotations a second; Murphy writes 'around 9 times per second'). Phase 1 (20 min) is the 20-min version; phase 2 makes it the 30-min version (a 60-min Shiva version also exists). The amygdala ('burstx') file is proprietary and approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) of 230 points x 3 ms followed by the standard 4-s latency (Murphy: standard signals use 3-ms points and a latency of about 4 s; the 230-point length is from Ryczko & Persinger 2002). Murphy suggests moving between temporal and frontal presentations over a series to keep frontal and temporal activity balanced, and trying a frontal session if a session feels good but you feel down afterwards. Persinger-lab studies reported that three weekly bilateral burst-firing sessions increased aggression and lowered trust (Gillis 1993) and that 20 min of burst-firing over the right temporoparietal lobe raised hypnotic suggestibility (Healey 1996). An independent randomized sham-controlled test of the 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal found no effect on emotional responses (Gendle & McGrath 2012), and a double-blind God Helmet test found no field effect (Granqvist 2005). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if distressed.
setting: Dark, quiet room, eyes closed, relaxed without meditating or falling asleep. Shiva offers 20, 30 and 60-min versions; start with the short one.
schedule: At most once a week, never on consecutive days; up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break. 60-min sessions weekly or every two weeks at most.
